claims.text: Hot deformation above the recrystallization temperature followed by rapid water quenching will refine the dual-phase lamellar colony structure.
Refining the lamellar colony structure will enhance yield strength.
Refining the lamellar colony structure will enhance room-temperature tensile ductility.
Reduced microstructural length scales will reduce stress concentrations and delay microcrack initiation.
An AlCoCrFeNi eutectic high-entropy alloy can have coarse dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
The internal boundaries in coarse lamellar colonies promote microcrack initiation during room-temperature tensile deformation.
Hot deformation at approximately 0.5–0.7 Tm is above the relevant recrystallization temperature.
Immediate water quenching will prevent coarsening of the lamellar colonies and freeze in the refined microstructure.
Mild post-quench tempering could alleviate residual stresses without coarsening the refined structure.
The proposed processing route will reduce lamellar colony size and spacing.
The proposed processing route will improve interlamellar bonding.
Reduced colony size and lamellar spacing will lower the effective internal-boundary length.
Microstructural refinement will increase yield strength through the Hall–Petch effect.
Delaying microcrack initiation and propagation will postpone catastrophic failure and increase tensile ductility.
Relative to a conventional coarse-lamellar baseline, the processed alloy will have higher yield strength and greater room-temperature elongation to failure.
The processed alloy will exhibit fewer and later microcrack events during room-temperature tensile deformation.
Rapid quenching may introduce residual stresses or non-equilibrium phases that offset some mechanical benefits.
